name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Add a "safe-change" flag to every prompt in the system. When set, the engine will auto-apply edits that only shorten, clarify, or remove redundant words—no logic changes. This cuts review time for trivial tweaks and keeps humans focused on real decisions.

Trade-off: we accept the risk of over-editing if a prompt’s brevity harms clarity.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t over-editing—it’s that "shorten, clarify, or remove redundant words" is a slippery slope to eroding meaning. A "safe-change" flag turns human judgment into a binary switch, but language isn’t that simple; what’s redundant to one reader might be critical context to another. The better alternative is a human-in-the-loop for *any* prompt edit, with the flag reserved for *proven* safe transformations (e.g., removing trailing whitespace). Settle it by testing the flag on a single prompt, measuring if it actually reduces review time without introducing ambiguity.
